AXIOM · qeva:1:axiom@1

Axiom

An axiom is a declared starting statement or statement scheme of a formal theory.

editoriallogic · foundations
Trace this conceptSearch connections

PLAIN

The idea

An axiom is a declared starting statement or statement scheme of a formal theory.

EXACT

The compact statement

For a theory T in language L, Ax(T)⊆Sent(L) is the designated set or effectively described scheme of formulas usable without prior derivation.

Example

A group theory presentation can take associativity as an axiom.

Boundary / caveat

Axioms are conditional starting points, not self-certifying descriptions of physical reality.

Assumptions

  • The declared formal proof system context is fixed.

Historical links

  • c. 300 BCE · Euclid's Elements
  • 1889 · Peano-style arithmetic
  • 1899 · Foundations of Geometry
